This map had a unique system of giving players cash for killing or damaging enemies. You only got cash from them if they are killed, or in some cases, damaged by a specific amount of health. Additionally, the amount you got is a set amount of cash, which was not always equal to the enemy's health. In solo, you received 100% of the cash when an enemy is killed or you damage it enough. With each additional player, this decreased by 25%, which means that in a quad, you only got 25% of the cash. This amount was distributed between players based on how much damage they dealt. However, if a player had not dealt any damage, they would receive 12.5% of the enemy's full cash upon its death or when it was damaged enough, regardless of player count. had three stages, all of which shared the same path layout, with all three stages having four paths. All three stages took place in a giant snow globe.

The first stage took place in a snow-blanketed town with Christmas and other holiday decor scattered around the houses and paths (gifts, string lights, snowfall etc.) Many of the houses had lights on in the windows suggesting that the town is inhabited by townsfolk celebrating the holidays. Additionally, there was a large Christmas tree in the center of the map with many icy cliffs nearby for cliff towers. The first stage occured from waves 0-9.
The second phase took place in a frozen-over outpost next to a stronghold that was taken over by

and its army. There were empty scouting towers on the outskirts that towers could be placed on with the frozen ones being unstable. There were little lampposts near the end of the paths along with many medium to large sized wooden cabins and many snowed-over trees around the cliffs and edges of the map. Most of the map was covered in snow and ice. The second stage occured from waves 10-17.

The third phase occured in an enclosed ice stronghold with a giant gateway that appears to be a portal. Intense snowfall covered the map as well as the icy, ancient architecture with most of it being arches or beams consistent with the style of the modern era Gothic or Neoclassical architecture. The gateway was made of ice and a bright light is shine through it signifying that it was a portal. There were lots of icy platforms for towers and tall brick towers for cliff towers to be placed on. The third stage occured from waves 18-20.
